title: Work
hook: work well, justly, and not endlessly
tomorrow: is money a blessing or a danger? Christians still argue it.

segments.voice: Yesterday, friends of other beliefs: Paul read the altar in Athens before he said a word. Your line was gentleness and respect. Today, a job that shows up surprisingly early.

Monday dread is practically its own genre: the alarm, the commute, the countdown to Friday. So here's an odd detail. In Genesis, work is not the punishment. Before anything goes wrong in the story, before the fruit, before the hiding, God puts the man in the garden of Eden “to dress it and to keep it.” A job, in paradise. And in the same chapter, a little earlier, God's own work comes to a stop. Why would a perfect garden need a gardener, and why would God need to stop?
screen: `MONDAY DREAD.` → `A JOB IN PARADISE.` → `WHY WOULD GOD STOP?`

segments.voice: Here's the solve. “And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made.” In this picture, work is good, and it has an end. The trouble comes later. Only after the disobedience does the ground bring thorns, and bread come in the sweat of the face. The curse lands on the toil, not on the tending. So today's hook gives work three edges. Work well: a garden is a real calling, and so is a classroom, a kitchen, a spreadsheet. Work justly: Jesus says “the labourer is worthy of his hire,” and James warns that wages “kept back by fraud” cry out. And work, but not endlessly. A psalm says it bluntly: “It is vain for you to rise up early, to sit up late, to eat the bread of sorrows: for so he giveth his beloved sleep.” Working late every night isn't proof of faithfulness, and sleep is called a gift. That's the odd detail solved. A gardener in paradise means work was made good. A God who stops means work was made to stop.
screen: `GOD ENDED HIS WORK, AND RESTED.` · `THE CURSE FALLS ON THE TOIL.` · `WELL, JUSTLY, NOT ENDLESSLY.` · `HE GIVETH HIS BELOVED SLEEP.` · then, large: `WORK AND REST.`

segments.voice: Name the time your work or study stops today. Name the one thing most likely to drag you past it, a last email, one more page, and decide now: when it shows up, I'll write it down for tomorrow and close the laptop. If you pray, you can hand the unfinished pile to God for the night.
Work. Tending what's in your hands, done well and fairly, with a stopping point, the way God's own work had one.
Pocket this one: work and rest, a gardener in Eden and a God who stopped. Day 1724, done.

howItsDone: Some Christians speak of their work as a vocation, a calling; churches keep the Lord's day for worship and rest in different ways, and some Christians set a firm stopping time for work each day.

fork.setup: your manager texts at 9 p.m.: can you finish the report tonight? it isn't urgent; it's due friday. by the three edges, what fits?
options: say yes; a faithful worker never stops early.
reply in the morning, and do it well before friday.
ignore it for good; work has nothing to do with faith.
fork.reveal: work well, work justly, and not endlessly: the report gets done well, and the night gets its rest.

original.note: the Hebrew verb behind 'he rested' in Genesis 2:2: to stop, to cease.

trapdoor: what you thought: work is the curse humans got for breaking the rules.
what it means: work is in the garden before anything goes wrong; what's cursed is the ground, and toil turns to sweat.
what a scholar hears: shavat, to stop or cease, is the verb in Genesis 2:2; God's rest is set beside human work before any law of sabbath is given.
guess: tending what's in your hands, well and fairly
a punishment handed down for the first sin
a duty to keep going until it's all done

chat.says: manager asked me to close AGAIN. fourth time this week. saying no feels lazy?? is it?
options: Not lazy. Work your shifts well, then stop. Even God's work had an end.
A little. Faithful workers say yes now and rest later, once things calm down.
Maybe it's the wrong job. If work wears you out, it isn't your calling.
chat.meaning: In Genesis work is good and has an edge: God ended his work and rested, and the psalm calls sitting up late vain.
